claim: Two members give opposite rules for whether SettlementForge's own assistant may set Find's chips. V10 §3.9b (7), new this round (l.1895-1897), says: 'A host's own assistant (configuration C) sets the chips as it sets any per-viewer view key, by §11.3's `view.set`'. V08 §3.16 (6) (g), new this round, says SettlementForge's assistant 'answers "where are the smiths" in words from the `gazetteer` query and sets no chip — no host message sets the frame's view but `view.set { week }`'. J-V8.127 records the choice ('to let SettlementForge's assistant answer in words without setting chips, over … a host message that drives the frame's Find … Find is the viewer's view, never the host's'). V08's repair handed this to V10 (repair-r1-V08.md HAND-OFFS: 'V10 (item 120): SettlementForge's assistant sets no Find chip (J-V8.127)'), but V10 had already landed with the opposite sentence. Configuration C is SettlementForge's assistant, so one host would both drive and not drive the frame's Find.
required_change: V10 §3.9b (7)'s last two sentences read: 'SettlementForge's own assistant (configuration C) sets no chip: it answers in words from the `gazetteer` query (V08 §3.16 (6) (g); J-V8.127), and a host proposal carries no find form.' V10 §3.17 adds no `find` path for a host.

claim: The clerk can propose an `advance` that a dossier-bound document refuses, and V10 has no words or alternative for it. V10 §4.1's T1 `intend` edit-mode row encodes `advance` as 'V06 §4.1's request, run on the scratch', with V06 §4.1's three shapes as its variations (V10 §3.11). V09 §4.3 names 'the clerk's proposal' as a route to `advance`. But §11.2 refuses `advance` on a dossier-bound document (V06 §2.3; J-V6.2), and nothing in V10 states this. V10 §3.16's `dossier` row names `refuse.dossierOwned`, `refuse.dossierRemove` and `refuse.roster.dossier` as its engine cases, not `refuse.dossierClock`. That row's only alternative, `button.whatIf` app(`openCopy` at the head, detached), is an `app` button. V10 §3.5 step 3 maps no `app` button: it says no dry-run row carries one. The clerk does have `fork` (V10 §2.6). So the canvas offers the what-if copy while the clerk's card either fails unworded or proposes an advance that cannot run. That breaks T101-3's 'one vocabulary'.
required_change: V10 §4.1's T1 `intend` edit-mode row: 'on a dossier-bound document no `advance` is encoded: the item is refused in V10 §3.16's `dossier` category with V09 §4.9's `refuse.dossierClock` (§11.2; V06 §2.3), its alternative a `fork` `ClerkAction` at the head, detached (V06 §4.4; V10 §2.6), worded by `button.whatIf`'. V10 §3.16's `dossier` row adds `refuse.dossierClock` among its engine cases with that alternative. V10 §3.5 step 3 adds 'a row's `app` button `openCopy` (`refuse.dossierClock`'s) maps to that `fork` action, the one `app` button a clerk card meets'. V10 §3.23 adds the edge (an advance asked on a dossier-bound document), tested in T-V10-50.

claim: The clerk's declaration step reads, from `edit`'s answer, fields §11.2's `ApplyResult` does not carry. V10 §3.5 step 3 runs `edit(scratch, events, { filtered: true })`. It then reads 'an answer carrying a `bent` `MsgRef` … its alternatives `propose` actions — for a placement bend each of the preview's plots', and step 4 returns 'its bend line …, its counts, its fates counted by kind …, its effects'. These also fill `DraftItem.bent`, `.counts`, `.fates`. §11.2's `ApplyResult` `ok` member is `{ status: 'ok'; logHead; changed; created }`, with no `bent`, `alternatives`, `counts` or `effects`. Its `confirm` member has fates and per-fate counts but no plot, household or building counts and no `bent`. Only `PreviewResult` carries `bent`, `alternatives`, `counts` and `effects`. A bent declaration that commits `ok` on the scratch therefore reaches the model with no bend line and no counts, and the item cannot become `bent`. This contradicts V10's own rule that a bent item is shown as bent (prompt rule 10, V10 §3.16).
required_change: V10 §3.5 step 3 reads: '`preview(scratch, events, { filtered: true })` — its `bent`, `alternatives`, `counts`, `fates`, `renames`, `effects` and, on `conflict`, its `outcome` and `actions` are the item's (a `refused` `role` answer the `role` refusal) — then, unless the preview is a `conflict` or `refused`, `edit(scratch, events)` with the preview's fates and renames filled (§11.2's resubmission form, as V10 §4.2 (1) commits), whose `created` names what the item made (item 470)'. V10 §6.1's declaration row counts the dry run with the commit.
